meta.pos: adj.; adv.; adj.; verb; adj.; noun; adj.

defs.def: forming a unit by itself; not joined to sth else 单独的；独立的；分开的

ex.s: After our third run Andrew shut down the engine, and we went our separate ways — he for a lunch break, I to explore the city.
ex.t: 第三趟航行结束后Andrew关掉发动机，我们各奔东西——他去吃午饭，我去探索这座城市。

ex.s: There is a separate bedroom, a modern kitchen with a refrigerator.
ex.t: 有一个独立的卧室，还有一个带冰箱的现代厨房。

ex.s: decision five years ago to create a separate set of standards for light sport aircraft, which are lower than those pilots of larger planes.
ex.t: 五年前做出的为轻型运动飞机制定一套单独标准的决定，这些标准低于大型飞机飞行员所需的标准。

ex.s: Mann said Terrafugia was helped by the Federal Aviation  Administration’s decision five years ago to create a separate set of standards for light sport aircraft, which are lower than those pilots of larger planes Terrafugia says an owner would need to pass a test and complete 20 hours of flying time to be able to fly the Transition, a requirement pilots would find relatively easy to meet.
ex.t: 曼说，Terrafugia得益于联邦航空管理局五年前做出的为轻型运动飞机制定一套单独标准的决定，这些标准低于大型飞机飞行员所需的标准。Terrafugia表示，车主需要通过一项测试并完成20小时的飞行时间才能驾驶Transition，飞行员会觉得这是很容易满足的要求。

ex.s: Over the last two years, some supermarkets   62   (start) selling chicken or salad in packs   63   (design) with two halves containing separate portions (份).
ex.t: 在过去两年里，一些超市开始销售鸡肉或沙拉，包装设计成两半，分别装有独立的份量。

ex.s: Then, on two separate morning visits to the scientists’ lab, each man walked for an hour at an average speed that, in theory should allow his body to rely mainly on fat for fuel.
ex.t: 随后，在两次分别前往科学家实验室的早晨探访中，每名男子都以平均速度走了一小时，这个速度理论上应能让身体主要依靠脂肪供能。

ex.s: This means that art and technology have always been seen as two very separate things.
ex.t: 这意味着艺术和技术一直被视为两个非常独立的事物。

ex.s: Superficially, these two men, whose lives were separated in time by nearly 1,500 years, were polar opposites.
ex.t: 从表面上看，这两个生活年代相隔近1500年的人是截然相反的。

ex.s: Last winter when I went here again, they had a big separate house to raise dozens of chicken.
ex.t: 去年冬天我再去了一次，他们有了一间独立的大屋，养了几十只鸡。

ex.s: In addition, the team set up a separate experiment that suggested that the baby birds that most closely imitated their mom’s voice were rewarded with the most food.
ex.t: 此外，研究团队还设立了一个独立的实验，表明那些模仿母亲声音最像的幼鸟得到了最多的食物。

defs.def: different; not connected 不同的；不相关的
to end a relationship with sb 断绝往来；分道扬镳
to go in a different direction from sb you have been travelling with 分路而行；分手
to divide into different parts or groups; to divide things into different parts or groups （使）分开，分离；分割；划分

ex.s: Used batteries are usually regarded as non-recyclable waste and should be disposed of separately.
ex.t: 废旧电池通常被视为不可回收垃圾，应当分开处理。

ex.s: Be prepared to be corrected by student B The classification of household waste aims to help people separate different types of waste.
ex.t: 为学生B的纠正做好准备生活垃圾的分类旨在帮助人们分离不同类型的垃圾。

ex.s: We began preparing the food, from mixing salad dressing to separating frozen meat.
ex.t: 我们开始准备食物，从调制沙拉酱到分拣冷冻肉类。

ex.s: Now separating / separated from her friends and her beloved hockey team, Riley starts to feel lost and helpless, and wants to run away from her parents and new school.
ex.t: 如今与她的朋友和她心爱的曲棍球队分开了，莱莉开始感到迷茫和无助，想要逃离她的父母和新学校。

defs.def: to move apart; to make people or things move apart （使）分离，分散
to be between two people, areas, countries, etc. so that they are not touching or connected 隔开；阻隔

ex.s: By interpreting the two definitions separately.
ex.t: 通过分别解释这两个定义。

defs.def: to stop living together as a couple with your husband, wife or partner 分居
to make sb/sth different in some way from sb/sth else 区分；区别
